Definition: , or (by variation) ἐκχύνω from G1537 and χέω (to pour); to pour forth; figuratively, to bestow:--gush (pour) out, run greedily (out), shed (abroad, forth), spill.
BiblicalUsage: To pour out is to empty a vessel, and the Bible uses it for blood, for the Spirit, and for love. Jesus says His blood is shed for many for the remission of sins, Peter says God will pour out His Spirit on all flesh in the last days, and Paul says the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost. The same word pours out judgement on the earth in Revelation, because God pours out whatever He gives, good or terrible, without holding back.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God pours out, never drips, because His blood, His Spirit, and His love are all given in full measure. I hold that the same fullness is what He asks of me, a life poured out, not measured.
RelatedTopics: Salvation; Outpouring of the Spirit; Love of God
